items.title: AWS Transform adds storage migration assessments for Amazon S3, EBS, EFS, and FSx
items.summary:
Migration assessments in AWS Transform now evaluate on-premises storage for migration to AWS. Instead of manually analyzing thousands of volumes across protocols, capacity, and performance, you upload a storage inventory and AWS Transform does the mapping for you. It matches each workload to the best-fit service, sizes the recommendation, and projects costs to produce a total cost of ownership business case. Bring NAS shares, SAN LUNs, direct-attached disks, or backup repositories via a NetApp Digital Advisor export, RVTools file, or other inventory. AWS Transform routes workloads across Amazon S3, Amazon EBS, Amazon EFS, and Amazon FSx (NetApp ONTAP, Windows File Server, OpenZFS, Lustre). Run what-if scenarios to compare deployment options such as Single-AZ vs. Multi-AZ or cost-optimized vs. performance-optimized, then ask follow-up questions about any result in chat.

Storage migration assessments are available in all AWS Regions where AWS Transform is available. To learn more, see the AWS Transform User Guide.

items.title: AWS Direct Connect announces 100G expansion in Manchester, England
items.summary:
Today, AWS announced the expansion of 10 Gbps and 100 Gbps dedicated connections with MACsec encryption capabilities at the existing AWS Direct Connect location in the Equinix MA3 data center near Manchester, England. You can now establish private, direct network access to all public AWS Regions (except those in China), AWS GovCloud Regions, and AWS Local Zones from this location. This is the third AWS Direct Connect location in England to provide 100 Gbps connections with MACsec encryption capabilities.

The Direct Connect service enables you to establish a private, physical network connection between AWS and your data center, office, or colocation environment. These private connections can provide a more consistent network experience than those made over the public internet.

For more information on the over 150 Direct Connect locations worldwide, visit the locations section of the Direct Connect product detail pages. Or, visit our getting started page to learn more about how to purchase and deploy Direct Connect.

items.title: Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS now support On-Demand Capacity Reservations
items.summary:
Starting today, you can reserve compute capacity for your Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS DB instances in one or more Availability Zones for as long as you need it. Reserving capacity helps ensure that DB instance create, restore, scale-compute, and start operations don't fail because of insufficient capacity.

On-Demand Capacity Reservations are designed for workloads that need assurance that specific DB instance capacity will be available when they need it for business-critical events, such as migrations, product launches, seasonal peaks, high-availability deployments, or disaster recovery. You choose the DB instance class, engine, Availability Zones, and reserved capacity per Availability Zone, and RDS holds that capacity for you. Capacity can be reserved in two or more Availability Zones to support Multi-AZ deployments. To use the reserved capacity, reference the reservation when you create, restore, modify, or start a DB instance.

You can reserve capacity for immediate use with no commitment and cancel at any time, or schedule a reservation to begin 5 to 120 days in the future with a minimum commitment. Reserved capacity is billed at On-Demand rates while the reservation is active, whether or not DB instances within the reservation are running. Discounts from your existing Reserved DB Instances or Database Savings Plans apply automatically.

On-Demand Capacity Reservations are available for Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS in all AWS commercial Regions. To learn more about On-Demand Capacity Reservations, visit the documentation for Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS.

items.title: Amazon Cognito extends multi-Region replication to AWS GovCloud (US) Regions
items.summary:
Amazon Cognito multi-Region replication (MRR) now supports AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, extending the resilience benefits of MRR to more workloads. MRR lets you synchronize user and machine identity data, including credentials, user pool configurations, and federation setups, to a secondary user pool in a standby Region you designate, in near real-time. With user data in the standby Region, you can redirect traffic and keep authentication available if there is a disruption in your primary Region.

Previously, MRR was available in 16 commercial Regions. You can now also use MRR to replicate between additional AWS Regions, helping you meet resilience, data residency, and compliance requirements in the Regions that best align with your business needs.

MRR is available as an add-on for user pools in the Essentials or Plus feature tiers, and requires a multi-Region AWS KMS customer managed key (CMK). For the full list of AWS Regions where Amazon Cognito is available, see AWS Capabilities by Region. To get started, visit the developer guide for instructions and the pricing page for pricing details.

items.title: Beam model by Reflection is now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart and AWS Trainium
items.summary:
Beam, the first open weight model offered by US-based Reflection, is now available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, the model hub in Amazon SageMaker AI. According to Beam, they operate at the frontier of open weight models in its class, with strong performance across reasoning, coding, and agentic benchmarks. Beam is for teams who build on and with an open weight model, not just call one. Customers who want to adapt a frontier model to their own domain can fine-tune it, inspect and modify its weights, and embed it deep in their agents and workflows, all while keeping full control of their data and infrastructure. Beam runs alongside other models that customers already use in SageMaker AI and scales to meet production demand with the same controls, audit trails, and monitoring built into every SageMaker AI deployment. Additionally, Beam was ported and optimized for AWS Trainium3, giving customers a high-performance, cost-efficient option for deploying and scaling the model from day one. “Reflection is delivering frontier AI that developers can actually control, not just rent through an API. Bringing Beam to SageMaker AI puts that capability in front of millions of developers on infrastructure they already trust, running in their own AWS account, on their own data, fully in their control," said Misha Laskin, co-founder and CEO, Reflection.

Teams building on Beam can take it well beyond calling an API: fine-tune it on proprietary code and data, specialize it for their own domains, and wire it into multi-step agentic workflows across their tools. In practice that means resolving real software issues, generating and reviewing code, automating operations work, and tackling advanced math and science reasoning on a model they can shape rather than one they simply consume. Because Beam is released under the Apache 2.0 license, customers can inspect and customize the model, while also running it in their own AWS accounts, so data stays private and under their control, protected by the same AWS security and compliance capabilities they already rely on. “Advanced AI models like Beam, now available on Amazon SageMaker, let us run open weight frontier AI entirely inside our own secure environments, with full visibility into the weights, the data, and the pipeline. In the age of multi-model AI, the pairing of openness and managed infrastructure is an essential addition to the AI ecosystem. The freedom to deploy and adapt advanced AI, tailored to mission problems with client-specific security and controls, gives more agencies greater flexibility to deploy advanced AI across their enterprise,” said Garrett Berntsen, Chief AI Officer, Accenture Federal Services.

Beam is initially available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart in US East (N. Virginia) and US East (Ohio). The model is available in BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 checkpoint variants, and can be deployed through a fully managed SageMaker JumpStart endpoint. To start, search for "Beam" in SageMaker JumpStart within Amazon SageMaker Studio, or deploy it directly on Sagemaker AI.  To learn more, read the AWS Machine Learning blog: Introducing Reflection Beam, SageMaker AI documentation and SageMaker JumpStart documentation for deployment guidance.

items.title: AWS Neuron 2.33 adds native PyTorch support, Neuron Observer, and other new features
items.summary:
AWS Neuron 2.33 is now available, introducing TorchNeuron, the native PyTorch backend for AWS Trainium, in public beta. You can run models written with the standard PyTorch APIs on Amazon EC2 Trn2 and Trn3 instances, in eager mode or with torch.compile. This release also introduces Neuron Observer in public beta, which detects Trainium health issues in under a second and identifies the affected node or device.

The vLLM Neuron plugin upgrades to vLLM 0.29.0, and the vLLM Omni Neuron plugin for Wan2.2 video generation is now part of the Neuron release. Both support native PyTorch compilation through TorchNeuron. A new Neuron Deep Learning AMI and Deep Learning Container for PyTorch training include TorchNeuron, PyTorch 2.14, and TorchTitan. Neuron Explorer opens profiles captured with torch.profiler. From a PyTorch memory snapshot, it now attributes allocations to the Python source lines that made them, for debugging out-of-memory errors in eager mode.

Kernels written with the Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) can now use the full Python language for metaprogramming, including generators and class inheritance. The NKI Library adds 25 new experimental kernels, including kernels for DeepSeek-V3.2, Qwen3.5, and Kimi Delta Attention.

To get started, see the following resources:

  • AWS Neuron 2.33.0 Release Notes

  • AWS TorchNeuron documentation

  • AWS Neuron Observer documentation

  • AWS Neuron Kernel Interface documentation

  • AWS Neuron

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer launches two new layouts for agent workspace
items.summary:
Amazon Connect Customer now offers two different layouts that optimize screen space on the agent workspace. Contact center agents spend hours each day in the agent workspace, which includes all of the contact controls and applications they need to resolve customer issues. Agents who handle different channels and workflows want the workspace arranged differently, so that they can quickly read, respond, and access their tools. Now, administrators can choose the best layout for each team, maximizing agent efficiency and satisfaction.

On the Modern layout, contact controls are at the top of the workspace, maximizing screen space for the applications beneath during voice calls. When agents handle chat, email, and task contacts on the Modern layout, they now have a taller, wider area to read and respond. The Classic layout offers a familiar experience for agents already using the agent workspace, now with contact controls that expand and contract by channel and a resizable agent assist application. Administrators can assign the Modern layout to a team migrating from another agent desktop with controls at the top, while teams already familiar with the agent workspace can use the Classic layout.

You can use the new layouts for the Amazon Connect Customer agent workspace in the following AWS regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Africa (Cape Town), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (London).

To learn more and get started, see the agent workspace in the Amazon Connect Customer administrator guide.

items.title: Amazon S3 server access log delivery to Amazon CloudWatch Logs now available in five additional AWS Regions
items.summary:
Amazon S3 server access log delivery to Amazon CloudWatch Logs is now available in the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, AWS European Sovereign Cloud, and AWS China Regions. With your access logs in CloudWatch Logs, you can query them as they arrive, set alarms, and encrypt them with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys. This new delivery path complements the existing delivery of server access logs to S3 general purpose buckets, giving you more flexibility in how you monitor and analyze access to your data.

With delivery to CloudWatch Logs, you can set alarms on error rates, monitor traffic patterns, investigate access incidents, and correlate S3 access activity with the rest of your operational data.

S3 server access log delivery to CloudWatch Logs is now available in all AWS Regions. Amazon CloudWatch Logs charges for vended logs apply. For pricing details, visit Amazon CloudWatch pricing. To learn more, visit the Amazon S3 User Guide.

items.title: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports custom sequence lengths for serverless model customization jobs
items.summary:
Today, Amazon SageMaker AI announces the ability to configure the sequence length used during your serverless model customization job. Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization supports fine-tuning for many open-weight models, including models from popular families including gpt-oss, Gemma, Llama, Nemotron, and Qwen. Previously, each fine-tuning recipe ran at a fixed sequence length that customers could not modify. Customers sometimes need to modify these parameters to achieve better results for their use case. Customers also asked for longer sequence lengths than the static defaults we supported on some models.

Now, you can set sequence length parameters as part of the customization job's hyperparameters, anywhere up to the published maximum for your chosen model and technique. You can set the dataset_max_len hyperparameter for SFT and DPO jobs or set max_prompt_length and max_response_length hyperparameters for RFT jobs. This gives you more control to match your training data characteristics, whether you are working with short question-answer pairs or multi-page documents. Published maximums are up to 16K tokens for many models depending on model and technique.

Serverless model customization on SageMaker AI is available in US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Europe (Ireland). To get started, navigate to the Models page in Amazon SageMaker Studio to launch a customization job, use the SageMaker Python SDK or use our Agent skills with your choice of coding assistant. To learn more, and see the list of models and supported sequence lengths per technique, see the SageMaker AI documentation.

items.title: AWS Network Firewall now supports Route 53 Resolved IP Validation
items.summary:
AWS Network Firewall now supports IP validation, extending domain-based filtering beyond HTTP/HTTPS to protocols such as SFTP and SSH. This new capability validates that a connection's destination IP address was resolved through your VPC's Amazon Route 53 VPC Resolver, closing security gaps where clients could bypass domain rules.

This feature enables Network Firewall customers to implement domain filtering rules for any protocol, not just HTTP/HTTPS, providing more flexible security policies than IP-based rules alone. It simplifies protection against Server Name Identifier (SNI) spoofing by validating the IPs resolved by the Route 53 VPC Resolver against the SNI, ensuring traffic only reaches legitimately resolved destinations. Organizations can now enforce consistent domain-based security policies across all outbound traffic types, from web applications to file transfer protocols, without complex workarounds. Additionally, Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall can be used with your VPC Resolver for extended DNS security.

Resolved IP validation is available in all AWS commercial regions where AWS Network Firewall and Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall are available, at no additional charge. For a full list of supported regions, visit the AWS Capabilities by Region page.

To learn more, visit AWS Network Firewall product page and service documentation.

items.title: Announcing Amazon ECS Gateway, a managed ingress solution for your ECS services
items.summary:
AWS announces Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) Gateway, a new resource that simplifies ingress networking for containerized applications by dynamically provisioning and managing Application Load Balancers (ALBs) and their supporting resources directly in your account.

With ECS Gateway, platform teams define organizational networking standards once on a gateway and associate it with one or more clusters, giving organizations a centralized way to govern how traffic reaches their ECS services. Application teams simply opt in to inherit those standards without requiring networking expertise. ECS Gateway offers host-based routing, allows up to 25 services to share an ALB to optimize infrastructure costs, and gives each service a unique Domain Name System (DNS) hostname. ECS manages the full lifecycle of the underlying infrastructure, provisioning the first ALB when your first service connects, adding more ALBs when capacity is reached, and removing them when no longer needed. You can inspect these resources and the gateway route to each service to see exactly how requests reach your applications. For traffic and health monitoring, you can use standard ALB metrics in Amazon CloudWatch and target health information from Elastic Load Balancing.

To get started, create an ECS Gateway, associate it with a cluster, and opt in your ECS service by adding the gateway connector parameter using the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, API, AWS SDKs, or AWS CloudFormation. ECS Gateway is available for ECS services using the awsvpc network mode across all launch types. It is available now in all commercial AWS Regions at no additional charge. You pay only for the underlying infrastructure provisioned in your account when your services connect to the gateway. To learn more, refer to the AWS News blog and our documentation page.

items.title: Amazon DynamoDB global tables now support disassociating replicas
items.summary:
Amazon DynamoDB global tables now support disassociating a replica without deleting its table or data. Global tables provide fully managed, multi-Region, multi-active replication. You can now stop replication to and from a replica and continue using the same table as a single-Region table.

An account can leave a shared multi-account global table and continue using its table independently. You can also stop replication to a Region while keeping its table for local workloads, validation, or audit, without creating a replacement table or copying data.

DynamoDB supports disassociating replicas in all AWS Regions for same-account and multi-account global tables that use multi-Region eventual consistency (MREC).

To get started, use the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, DynamoDB API, or AWS CloudFormation. For more information, see Disassociating replicas in the Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide.

items.title: Amazon WorkSpaces simplifies secure AI agent access to enterprise cloud desktops with less infrastructure to operate and manage
items.summary:
WorkSpaces for AI agents now handles authentication and desktop connections as part of the managed Model Context Protocol (MCP) service, so you can connect agents to governed cloud desktops, removing the need to write custom code. This makes it easy to use WorkSpaces with any client that supports MCP.

Connecting an agent to a desktop previously required you to manage presession requirements; generate, invoke, and rotate streaming URLs manually, adding complexity every time a session expired. You can now create sessions with your existing AWS credentials through OAuth 2.0, and the service handles the connection lifecycle. You configure once which desktop stack to use, and your agents reach the right desktop without ever seeing or handling the underlying streaming connection. You can also query session state to see which desktop stack, fleet, and session an agent is connected to, and generate a link for real-time observability of your agent. This gives you visibility and auditability over active agent work to know what your agents are doing and where.

To help your agents work with multiple applications, they can now discover and launch applications through a catalog MCP Tool rather than navigating menus. Using these new tools, agents can list the available applications, launch one or several at runtime, and switch between them, replacing the start-menu and taskbar navigation with a programmatic, deterministic path that improves accuracy and reduces token cost. 

WorkSpaces for AI agents runs agent sessions inside the same network isolation and compliance boundaries that govern your human workforce, inheriting the VPC controls, data-loss prevention policies, and session-level security posture that enterprises have already configured. The service is also now available in four additional AWS Regions: South America (São Paulo), Europe (Milan), Europe (Spain), and Asia Pacific (Malaysia).

To get started operating AI agents on WorkSpaces, visit: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appstream2/latest/developerguide/agent-access.html.

items.title: Polly Generative engine upgraded with more natural speech, 14 new voices, and 2 new languages
items.summary:
Today, we are introducing a new model behind the Amazon Polly Generative engine that delivers more natural-sounding, accurate speech output with low latency. With this upgrade, you get access to an enhanced voice portfolio with higher overall quality, 14 new voices across nine locales, and two new languages—Hindi and Finnish—now generally available on the Generative engine for the first time. New voices include Kenneth and Nate (US English), Russell and Curtis (Australian English), Kiara and Arjun (Hindi and Indian English), Tina (German), Carlos (US Spanish), Leo and Carolina (Brazilian Portuguese), Hyunduk (Korean), and Suvi (Finnish).

Amazon Polly is a fully managed service that turns text into natural-sounding speech. This drop-in model upgrade makes Generative voices more natural and accurate. Complex content such as numbers, email addresses, and street addresses is designed to sound more reliable, reducing the need to fine-tune speech output. You can continue to use Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML) tags to control speech output on the Generative engine, just as before. The low-latency streaming API makes it easy to build contact center experiences, chatbots, and large language model (LLM) based agentic voice applications for real-time conversations. The richness and variety of voice options are also well suited for news, media, entertainment, e-learning, and accessibility use cases. This launch also expands the Amazon Polly Generative offering to AWS GovCloud, providing more options for public sector and regulated industries.

All new Generative voices are now available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Zurich), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Canada (Central), and AWS GovCloud (US-West).

To hear how Polly voices sound, go to Amazon Polly Features. For more details on the Polly offerings and use, see the Amazon Polly documentation and pricing page.

items.title: AWS announces TorchNeuron: Native PyTorch Support for AWS Trainium (Public Beta)
items.summary:
Today, AWS launched the public beta of TorchNeuron, an open source native PyTorch backend for AWS Trainium. Trainium is a portfolio of AI chips designed to deliver high performance and cost efficiency for deep learning AI training and inference workloads. TorchNeuron enables AI scientists and researchers to experiment and build models with PyTorch natively on Trainium.

With TorchNeuron, developers can enable their PyTorch code on Trainium simply by switching to .to('neuron') while maintaining full PyTorch compatibility with eager execution, torch.compile, and standard PyTorch APIs. Additionally, TorchNeuron integrates with Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) to enable custom operators and performance optimization for Trainium hardware.

TorchNeuron is available as open source through the TorchNeuron github repo for Amazon EC2 Trainium2 instances and Amazon EC2 Trainium3 instances.

To learn more about TorchNeuron and AWS Trainium accelerators, visit the AWS Neuron page.

items.title: Structured outputs for Claude models available on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary:
Amazon Bedrock now supports structured outputs for all Anthropic Claude models across both the bedrock-runtime and the bedrock-mantle endpoint. Whether you call Claude through boto3 and the bedrock-runtime APIs or through the Messages API and the bedrock-mantle endpoint, you can now receive schema-compliant JSON responses that conform to a defined structure, without custom parsing, retry logic, or post-processing.

With structured outputs for Claude on Amazon Bedrock, you can automate reliable, schema-compliant tasks across industries. Examples include extracting every required field from financial earnings reports and compliance documents, parsing clinical notes into Electronic Health Records (EHR), and enriching product catalogs with consistent, validated results. You can also analyze contracts for key terms, parties, and obligations, or power intelligent support ticket routing where intents, sentiments, and entities always match your application's data model.

To learn more, see the Amazon Bedrock documentation . Structured outputs is available where claude models are available. For more information check the regional availability details page.

items.title: AWS Clean Rooms now supports Databricks as a data source
items.summary:
AWS Clean Rooms now supports Databricks as a data source, so collaboration members and their partners can securely analyze data managed in Databricks without moving or revealing the source data. Members query a Databricks table shared through Delta Sharing directly in a collaboration. Databricks joins AWS Glue, Snowflake, and Amazon Athena as supported data sources in AWS Clean Rooms.

Previously, members with data in Databricks had to export or replicate it into Amazon S3 to use it as a table in a collaboration, which added pipeline work and an extra copy of the data to govern. Now members can register a Databricks table directly by providing the workspace URL, schema, and table along with a Delta Sharing share, and make it available to a collaboration. For example, a retailer that manages its customer data in Databricks can collaborate with a media partner on campaign measurement in AWS Clean Rooms, running approved analyses against its Databricks data without first building and maintaining an export to S3.

AWS Clean Rooms helps companies and their partners easily analyze and collaborate on their collective datasets without revealing or copying one another’s underlying data. For more information about the AWS Regions where AWS Clean Rooms is available, see the AWS Regions table. To learn more about collaborating with AWS Clean Rooms, visit AWS Clean Rooms.

items.title: AWS IAM Identity Center simplifies identity source changes from Active Directory
items.summary:
AWS IAM Identity Center now retains your workforce identities and their assignments when you change your identity source from Active Directory to an external identity provider (IdP), such as Okta or Microsoft Entra ID, or to the Identity Center directory. Specifically, it preserves your users, groups, group memberships, permission set assignments, and application assignments. Previously, this change required you to recreate them in IAM Identity Center.

IAM Identity Center helps you connect your workforce identities to AWS once and manage their access centrally across AWS applications and accounts. When you change your identity source from Active Directory, your existing identity store remains in place, so your users and groups keep the same IDs. As a result, users retain their access to AWS accounts and applications, and policies that reference your user IDs, group IDs, or identity store ID continue to work.

To make this change, configure your new identity source with the standard setup required for users to sign in. After the change, your workforce signs in through your dual-stack AWS access portal URL. Changing your identity source in the other direction, to Active Directory, works as before. This feature is available for organization instances of IAM Identity Center in all AWS Regions where IAM Identity Center is available. IAM Identity Center is provided at no additional cost.

To get started, navigate to the IAM Identity Center console. For more information, see Change your identity source in the IAM Identity Center User Guide. To learn more about IAM Identity Center, visit the product detail page.

items.title: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails now supports Standard tier for contextual grounding checks
items.summary:
Amazon Bedrock Guardrails now offers a Standard tier for contextual grounding checks, which detect and filter hallucinations by checking whether a model response is grounded in your reference source and relevant to the user's query. The Standard tier is more robust than the Classic tier. It supports responses that include reasoning or conversational content, scores differently worded responses with the same meaning more consistently, and provides more comprehensive language support, matching the Standard tier for content filters and denied topics. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails provides configurable safeguards for generative AI applications on any foundation model through the ApplyGuardrail API.

Until now, contextual grounding checks applied strict grounding suited to summarization, paraphrasing, and question answering. With the Standard tier, you can also apply contextual grounding checks to conversational applications and to responses that reason over the source. You choose the tier for each guardrail in the Amazon Bedrock console or API. Existing guardrails keep the Classic tier until you change them. Pricing is the same for both tiers. To use the Standard tier, your guardrail must use cross-Region inference with a guardrail profile.

The Standard tier for contextual grounding checks is available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (N. California), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Ireland), Europe (Milan), Europe (Paris), Europe (Spain), Europe (Stockholm), and Asia Pacific (Tokyo). To learn more, see the Amazon Bedrock Guardrails documentation on contextual grounding checks and safeguard tiers, or visit the Amazon Bedrock Guardrails product page.

items.title: AWS Partner Central launches Program Navigator, Case Study Generator, and streamlined specialization review
items.summary:
AWS Partner Central now features Program Navigator, a unified experience that lets partners discover, apply for, and track AWS Specialization program applications in one place. Partners can browse specialization designations, view requirements and benefits, and submit applications through a guided, step-by-step workflow.

The new Case Study Generator in AWS Partner Central gives partners a redesigned creation experience with three starting paths: build a case study directly with AI assistance, import from an existing customer success story URL, or auto-populate from an opportunity. Case studies created for go-to-market purposes now follow a streamlined review path, a lightweight policy validation that lets partners publish directly to AWS domains without a specialization review. The deeper specialization-level review applies only to case studies associated with Program Navigator applications.

Additionally, AWS has streamlined the specialization application review process through Program Navigator. Partners submitting applications can expect faster review times and more detailed, requirement-level feedback throughout the process. Partners applying for non-specialization programs continue to access those programs through the existing experience.

Program Navigator and Case Study Generator are available to all AWS Partners in AWS Partner Central. To get started, navigate to Program Navigator and Case Studies under the Go to Market section in the left navigation panel.

items.title: Amazon Bedrock Advanced Prompt Optimization now supports prompt shortening
items.summary:
Amazon Bedrock Advanced Prompt Optimization now supports prompt shortening, an optional setting that reduces the length of your prompt while maintaining or improving your evaluation scores. Advanced Prompt Optimization optimizes prompts for any model on Amazon Bedrock against your own evaluation criteria. Until now, optimization focused on quality alone. Optimized prompts were often longer than the original. Longer prompts raise input token costs and can increase time to first token, which matters at scale and in latency-sensitive applications.

When you turn on prompt shortening for a prompt template in your input dataset, the optimizer reduces the prompt's length. The optimized prompt is returned only when it is shorter than your original prompt and scores at least as high on your evaluation. Otherwise your original prompt is returned, so the setting never leaves you with a longer or lower-scoring prompt. Results include a compression ratio and the original and optimized token counts, in the output file and on the console results page. For example, a compression ratio of 0.7 means the optimized prompt uses 30% fewer tokens. Prompt shortening works with any evaluation method, including steering criteria, LLM-as-a-judge rubrics, and custom Lambda evaluators.    

Prompt shortening is available in all AWS Regions where Advanced Prompt Optimization is available. To get started, enable prompt shortening for a prompt template in your input dataset and create an optimization job as usual. To learn more, see Shorten prompts in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide, the Amazon Bedrock pricing page, and the Amazon Bedrock product page.

items.title: AWS Transform for migrations expands support for existing landing zones
items.summary:
AWS Transform now supports more types of existing AWS environments when building landing zones for your migration, including AWS Control Tower landing zones and landing zones built with AWS Organizations. AWS Transform runs a foundation gap analysis of your current environment against AWS best practices and expands your landing zone on top of what's already in your target accounts, so your team can start migrating sooner.

AWS Transform also now supports an Infrastructure as Code (IaC)-only mode for building landing zones for your migration. In this mode, AWS Transform analyzes your organization, generates recommendations, and produces IaC tailored to your migration plan in AWS CDK, Terraform, or Landing Zone Accelerator (LZA) format. IaC-only mode is designed for organizations that prefer not to grant AWS Transform direct access to their management account. AWS Transform can now connect through a delegated administrator (DA) account instead. It also benefits customers who manage their own deployment pipeline and don't need the agent to deploy automatically.

The AWS Transform for migrations landing zone agent automates landing zone design end to end, including foundation setup, organizational unit (OU) and account structure, service control policies (SCPs), and workload accounts aligned to your migration planning and waves. You can deploy directly or generate IaC for your own pipeline.

These new capabilities are available in all target AWS Regions supported by AWS Transform for migrations.

To learn more, please visit the AWS Transform User Guide.

items.title: Amazon CloudWatch Alarms now supports tags in alarm actions payload
items.summary:
Today, Amazon CloudWatch announces support for including alarm tags in action payloads and Amazon EventBridge events, enabling customers to route and filter alarm notifications by tag without additional lookups. When enabled on an alarm, CloudWatch adds the alarm tags to the messages it sends to Amazon SNS, AWS Lambda, and Amazon EventBridge each time the alarm changes state. This option is designed for customers who route many alarms through a shared notification pipeline and need to identify the owning team, environment, or service directly from the message.

With tags in actions payloads, customers can avoid the extra work of correlating tag metadata with alarm events after the fact. For example, a team that routes hundreds of alarms through a single SNS topic to a Lambda function previously had to call ListTagsForResource for each event to find the owning team before paging. With this feature, the tags arrive in the notification, so the function can route directly from the message. The setting is off by default and configurable per alarm, and customers can include all tags, only selected tag keys, or all tags except selected keys. It is supported for metric, composite, and log alarms.

Tags in actions and events for CloudWatch Alarms are available in all AWS Regions where Amazon CloudWatch is available except Middle East (UAE), and Middle East (Bahrain).

To get started, see  Alarm tags in action payloads  in the Amazon CloudWatch User Guide. To learn more about Amazon CloudWatch Alarms, visit the  Amazon CloudWatch  product page.

items.title: Amazon ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey now supports online migration with zero downtime
items.summary:
Amazon ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey now supports online migration from self-managed Valkey and Redis OSS on Amazon EC2 with zero downtime. Zero downtime means zero Errors returned to the client during migration, measured the same way the ElastiCache SLA measures availability. Your application continues reading and writing through cutover, and you do not need third-party replication tools.

Online migration runs in three steps. You prepare the migration, start the data sync, and complete the cutover. ElastiCache gives you a migration endpoint your application can point to when you prepare the migration, and data replicates continuously from your source once you start the sync. You choose when writes move to the serverless cache, with a manual cutover or an automatic one once your data is in sync. ElastiCache records each step as an event on the cache’s Events tab, with the reason for any failed step.

Online migration connects to your source using encryption in transit (TLS) and authentication, and reads credentials from AWS Secrets Manager, so your existing security controls stay in place. Online migration supports self-managed caches in cluster mode on Amazon EC2 running Redis OSS 4.0 through 7.2 or Valkey 7.2 through 8.1, and you can migrate them straight to Valkey 9.0.

Migration usage is free for the first 180 days per AWS account, starting when the account first prepares a migration. After that, you pay per node-hour for the migration nodes that ElastiCache runs to replicate your data, for as long as a migration is active. The ElastiCache Serverless cache is billed separately at standard data storage and ECPU rates, including during the free period. For pricing details, see Amazon ElastiCache pricing. Online migration is available in all commercial AWS Regions, the China Regions, and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. 

To get started, create or select an empty ElastiCache Serverless cache to migrate into, then start the migration from the ElastiCache console or the AWS CLI. To learn more, see the documentation.

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer Global Resiliency now provides business users visibility into resiliency readiness across linked Regions
items.summary:
Amazon Connect Customer Global Resiliency now provides a Global Resiliency page in the admin website, giving administrators a single place to review their Region switch readiness. The page shows an overall readiness status and lists the resources that Global Resiliency natively replicates, including which resource types are in sync, which are still pending synchronization, and which need action. For example, if a phone number or user is not associated with a traffic distribution group, the page flags it and lets the administrator associate the affected resources directly from the page. With this readiness overview, administrators can review their resiliency posture at any time and verify that their instance is ready for a Region switch.

This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Connect Customer Global Resiliency is supported. To learn more, see Amazon Connect Customer admin guide.

items.title: Amazon CloudWatch Omni is now available in additional AWS Regions
items.summary:
AWS announces that Amazon CloudWatch Omni is now available in eight additional AWS Regions. CloudWatch Omni is an AI-powered observability experience, organized around your teams and the applications they run, that helps you observe and troubleshoot your applications and agents in one place. It combines the interoperability of OpenTelemetry with the scale and reliability of CloudWatch, and meets you where you work — a standalone web experience with single sign-on (SSO), or a local IDE extension.

With CloudWatch Omni, You create spaces in your central accounts to see telemetry across your AWS accounts, Regions, and other clouds, including Azure and GCP. Omni discovers services, maps dependencies, and surfaces golden metrics automatically and you can interact with telemetry through chat, point-and-click, or your own tool via Agent Toolkit for AWS to find signals, build dynamic views, and reach root cause powered by AWS DevOps Agent. A dedicated agent observability experience adds an evaluation-driven workflow for frameworks including LangGraph, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, Vercel AI SDK, and Strands.

With this expansion, CloudWatch Omni is now available in Canada (Central), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), and South America (São Paulo), in addition to US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), and Europe (Ireland).

To get started, create your Omni space from the CloudWatch console, configure SSO, and sign in. Agent developers can install the free CloudWatch Omni extension for VS Code, Cursor, and Kiro. To learn more, see the Amazon CloudWatch Omni product page and documentation. For pricing, see the CloudWatch Omni pricing page.

items.title: EC2 Image Builder now integrates with ASG for faster image builds
items.summary:
EC2 Image Builder now supports using existing instances from an Auto Scaling Group (ASG) for building images, enabling faster builds by eliminating the time spent in launching and bootstrapping new instances and reusing already running EC2 instances.

With this feature, you can provide an ASG in your Image Builder infrastructure configuration. Instead of launching a new instance at the build time, Image Builder selects an already-running instance from this ASG, applies your build components, and creates the image. The ASG continuously replenishes the pool as instances are used for builds, ensuring instances are always available for subsequent pipeline runs.

This feature is fully opt-in and does not affect existing pipelines. Pipelines without an ASG configured continue to use the default launch path with no behavior change.

This feature is available in all AWS Regions at no additional cost. To configure ASG integration in your Image Builder pipelines, see the EC2 Image Builder documentation.

items.title: Amazon GuardDuty adds optional threat detection rules for Runtime Monitoring
items.summary:
Amazon GuardDuty now supports optional detection rules for Runtime Monitoring. You can enable more than 50 Runtime Monitoring rules that help detect process, file, and network activity that might be routine in one environment but a sign of compromise in another, such as modifying sudoers files or disabling audit logging.

The new rules provide detections for Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon EKS, and Amazon ECS on both EC2 and AWS Fargate, and span 13 finding types mapped to MITRE ATT&CK® tactics including persistence, privilege escalation, execution, defense evasion, discovery, exfiltration, and command and control. This release introduces four new finding types: CommandAndControl:Runtime/SuspiciousCommand, CredentialAccess:Runtime/SensitiveFileRead, Discovery:Runtime/SensitiveFileRead, and Exfiltration:Runtime/SuspiciousCommand.

To get started, visit the GuardDuty console. You can enable rules in dry-run mode to evaluate detection efficacy before enabling live detection.

Custom Detection Rules for Runtime Monitoring is available in all AWS commercial Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To learn more, see Amazon GuardDuty Custom Detection Rules. To receive programmatic updates on new Amazon GuardDuty features and threat detections, subscribe to the Amazon GuardDuty SNS topic.

items.title: Grok 4.7 is now available on Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US)
items.summary:
Amazon Bedrock now supports SpaceXAI Grok 4.7, a frontier model built for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work in AWS GovCloud (US).

Grok 4.7 builds on Grok 4.6 with better mixed-document handling, more dependable repo-scale coding with planning and error recovery, and enhanced browser-use agents for form fills and portal navigation.  

Get started with Grok 4.7 in the Amazon Bedrock console or programmatically through supported Amazon Bedrock APIs. For information about supported AWS Regions, endpoints, APIs, features, inference profiles and pricing, see the Amazon Bedrock documentation. To learn more, read the launch blog post.

items.title: AWS IAM Identity Center now supports optimistic locking for users and groups in its identity store
items.summary:
IAM Identity Center helps you configure the single sign-on experience of your workforce to AWS accounts and applications. You can now use optimistic locking for users and groups in the identity store, so that update and delete requests succeed only if the user or group hasn't changed since you last read it. This helps when multiple administrators or automated workflows modify the same user or group at nearly the same time, where previously one write could silently overwrite another.

Each user and group now has a Revision value that changes every time the user's or group's attributes are modified, including through SCIM provisioning, Active Directory sync, or the IAM Identity Center console. Create, describe, update, and list operations return the current Revision, and you can pass it on a later UpdateUser, UpdateGroup, DeleteUser, or DeleteGroup request. The request succeeds only if the supplied Revision matches the current Revision. Otherwise, it returns a ConflictException, so your workflow can re-read the user or group and retry with the latest values.

Providing a Revision is optional. Requests that omit it behave as before, so existing integrations continue to work without changes. Conditional requests are supported through the Identity Store API, not the SCIM endpoint. Group membership operations don't accept a Revision, and adding or removing members doesn't change the Revision of the user or the group. This capability is available in all AWS Regions where IAM Identity Center is available. IAM Identity Center is provided at no additional cost.

To learn more about IAM Identity Center, visit the product detail page. To get started, see UpdateUser in the Identity Store API Reference.

items.title: AWS Elemental MediaConnect Router now supports high bitrate mode
items.summary:
AWS Elemental MediaConnect Router now supports high bitrate modes with two new tiers: 250 Mbps and 500 Mbps. This allows professional broadcasters that need higher bitrates to transport high-value content without compromising quality or reliability.

This enhancement enables industry-standard workflows such as VSF TR-07 compliant transport stream distribution for broadcast contribution, content distribution, and remote production. High bitrate mode supports up to two redundant sources for reliability and includes data plane optimizations that reduce jitter for improved performance.

To learn more, visit the AWS Elemental MediaConnect product page and the MediaConnect pricing page.

items.title: Amazon RDS Custom now supports the latest Cumulative Update and GDR updates for Microsoft SQL Server
items.summary:
Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) Custom for SQL Server now supports the latest Cumulative Updates (CU) and General Distribution Release (GDR) updates for Microsoft SQL Server. This release includes support for SQL Server 2019 CU32+GDR KB5122772(RDS version 15.00.4490.9.v1) and SQL Server 2022 CU26 + GDR KB5122768 (RDS version 16.00.4275.2.v1).

For additional information on the improvements and fixes included in these updates, see Microsoft documentation for KB5122772 and KB5122768. You can upgrade your Amazon RDS Custom for SQL Server instances to apply these recommended updates using Amazon RDS Management Console, or by using the AWS SDK or CLI. To learn more about upgrading your database instances, see Amazon RDS Custom User Guide.

items.title: Amazon RDS for SQL Server now supports snapshots on read replicas
items.summary:
Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for SQL Server now supports creating DB snapshots directly on read replica instances. Previously, you could create snapshots only on standalone and primary DB instances. You can now snapshot a read replica without promoting it first, giving you more flexibility in your backup and disaster recovery (DR) workflows.

Previously, enabling Multi-AZ on a promoted read replica meant waiting for an initial full snapshot to finish before the conversion could begin. On larger storage configurations—such as io2 volumes up to 64 TiB—that first snapshot could take a long time, making DR timelines hard to predict. Now, Amazon RDS for SQL Server maintains snapshot data on the read replica throughout its lifecycle, so the first snapshot after promotion completes faster. This shortens the time to enable Multi-AZ and helps you plan DR exercises with more predictable recovery timelines. You can take manual snapshots of a read replica, turn on automated backups by setting a backup retention period greater than zero, and retain automated backups when you delete the replica; however, point-in-time recovery (PITR) from a read replica isn't supported.

This feature works for both in-region and cross-region read replicas. It's available for SQL Server Enterprise Edition on all SQL Server versions that support read replicas, in all AWS Regions where Amazon RDS for SQL Server read replicas are available, including the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions.

To learn more, see Working with read replicas for Microsoft SQL Server. For pricing details, see Amazon RDS for SQL Server Pricing.

items.title: AWS Partner Central adds Solution Matching Engine performance insights
items.summary:
AWS Partner Central now gives AWS Partners more visibility into how the Solution Matching Engine (SME) contributes to their co-sell pipeline. The Solution Matching Engine performance section in Partner Analytics helps partners understand how SME performs for their company and AWS Marketplace listings.

Partners can view recommendations, SME-attributed opportunities, their share of AWS-originated opportunities, stall rate, and pipeline attributed to SME. They can filter by recommendation type or AWS Marketplace listing and explore top customer profiles by Region, industry, and segment. These insights help partners assess their visibility and decide where to improve their listings and opportunity information.

All partners eligible for APN Customer Engagements (ACE) can find the section on the Opportunity pipeline analysis page under Partner Analytics in AWS Partner Central. To learn more about SME and how to strengthen your visibility with AWS sellers, read Solution Matching Engine: Your Gateway to AWS Sellers.

items.title: Amazon CloudWatch log centralization now available in AWS GovCloud and additional commercial Regions
items.summary:
Amazon CloudWatch log centralization is now available in AWS GovCloud (US) and 13 additional commercial Regions. CloudWatch log centralization copies log data from multiple AWS accounts and Regions into a single destination account, integrating with AWS Organizations for efficient aggregation without the need for custom solutions.

With this launch, organizations in the AWS GovCloud (US) partition and commercial partition can each centralize logs across their accounts and Regions for centralized monitoring. You can scope centralization rules to your entire organization, specific organizational units, or selected accounts and copy logs into a single account while preserving source context through enriched system fields.

CloudWatch log centralization is now additionally available in Africa (Cape Town), Asia Pacific (Hong Kong), Asia Pacific (Hyderabad), Asia Pacific (Jakarta), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Asia Pacific (Melbourne), Canada West (Calgary), Europe (Milan), Europe (Spain), Europe (Zurich), Israel (Tel Aviv), Middle East (Bahrain), Middle East (UAE), AWS GovCloud (US-East), and AWS GovCloud (US-West). For a complete list of supported Regions, see the AWS Region table.

To get started, create a centralization rule in the Amazon CloudWatch console, or by using the AWS CLI or AWS SDKs. To learn more, see Log centralization in the Amazon CloudWatch Logs User Guide. Customers can centralize one copy of logs for free; additional copies are charged at $0.05/GB. For details, see Amazon CloudWatch pricing.

items.title: Amazon EMR Serverless now supports IPv6 and dual-stack connectivity
items.summary:
Amazon EMR Serverless now supports IPv6 and dual-stack connectivity, expanding beyond the IPv4-only connectivity that was previously available. You can now run your Apache Spark and Apache Hive jobs over IPv6 in your Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) by supplying dual-stack (IPv4 and IPv6) or IPv6-only subnets. This gives you greater flexibility in how your applications connect to data stores and services, while maintaining full backward compatibility with your existing IPv4 workloads.

As Spark and Hive workloads scale to many workers, the IPv4 address space in your VPCs and subnets can become a constraint, and a growing number of organizations face compliance mandates that require IPv6 adoption. With dual-stack connectivity, your EMR Serverless applications accept both IPv4 and IPv6, making it easy to adopt IPv6 gradually while maintaining backward compatibility with your existing IPv4 workloads. With IPv6-only subnets, you can eliminate the need for IPv4 addresses entirely, overcoming IPv4 address exhaustion and meeting the networking standards and compliance requirements that call for IPv6, while your jobs reach IPv6 endpoints and services both inside and outside your VPC.

IPv6 and dual-stack connectivity for Amazon EMR Serverless is available at no additional cost in all AWS Regions where Amazon EMR Serverless is available. IPv6 and dual-stack subnets are supported on all EMR Serverless release versions. To get started, see Configure IPv6 subnets for EMR Serverless applications and Configuring VPC access for EMR Serverless applications.

items.title: AWS Lambda durable functions are now available in AWS GovCloud (US) Regions
items.summary:
AWS Lambda durable functions are now available in the AWS GovCloud (US-West) and AWS GovCloud (US-East) Regions. Lambda durable functions enable developers to build reliable multi-step applications and AI workflows within the Lambda developer experience.

Lambda durable functions extend the Lambda programming model with new primitives in your event handler, such as "step" and "wait", allowing you to checkpoint progress, automatically recover from failures, and pause executions without incurring compute charges for on-demand functions. With availability in the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, government customers and regulated industries can orchestrate complex processes such as order workflows, user onboarding, and AI-assisted tasks while meeting stringent compliance and security requirements.

You can activate durable functions for new Python (versions 3.13 and 3.14), Node.js (versions 22 and 24), Go (versions 1.24 or later), .Net (version 2.2), or Java (17+) based Lambda functions using the AWS Lambda API, AWS Management Console, or AWS SDK. You can also use infrastructure as code tools such as AWS CloudFormation, AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM), and the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK).

For more information on durable functions, visit the AWS Lambda durable functions product page or the AWS Lambda Developer Guide. To learn about pricing, visit AWS Lambda pricing. For region availability, visit the AWS Capabilities by Region page.

items.title: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL model now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
items.summary:
NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, expanding the portfolio of foundation models available to AWS customers. This vision-language model from the Nemotron 3.5 family accepts images, video, and text as input and generates text, enabling customers to deploy multimodal AI solutions on AWS infrastructure.

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is designed for document intelligence, GUI understanding, video question answering, and multimodal agentic applications. It pairs a 120B-parameter hybrid Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language backbone with 12B active parameters and a vision encoder, supporting context lengths of up to 1 million tokens. The model includes a built-in Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) head for speculative decoding to accelerate text generation, with reasoning configurable per request. It supports ten languages including English, French, Spanish, German, Japanese, Hindi, Korean, and Chinese. Post-trained with multimodal supervised fine-tuning on image, video, document, chart, and GUI data followed by GRPO reinforcement learning, it delivers structured JSON output, tool calling, and configurable reasoning for enterprise agent workflows. SageMaker JumpStart offers two variants: NVFP4 for optimized inference on G7 instances with NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, and BF16 reference weights on ml.p5en.48xlarge for customization including SFT, RL, distillation, and domain adaptation.

With SageMaker JumpStart, customers can deploy Nemotron 3.5 Super VL with just a few clicks to address their specific AI use cases.

To get started with these models, navigate to the SageMaker JumpStart model catalog in the SageMaker console or use the SageMaker Python SDK to deploy the models to your AWS account. For more information about deploying and using foundation models in SageMaker JumpStart, see the Amazon SageMaker JumpStart documentation.

items.title: AWS Transform announces Azure-to-AWS cloud-native code conversion
items.summary:
Today, AWS announced the general availability of application code conversion from Azure SDK to AWS SDK in AWS Transform, giving you an accelerated path to migrate Microsoft Azure cloud-native .NET applications to AWS. The AWS Transform .NET modernization agent identifies Azure service code and converts it to equivalent AWS service code. For example, an Azure Functions serverless function that uses Azure Cosmos DB can be converted to an AWS Lambda function that uses Amazon DynamoDB.

AWS Transform discovers the Azure SDK in your submitted source code and presents the conversion options in the assessment report and modernization plan. You can accept the options provided or adjust them based on your preferences before running the modernization. AWS Transform then converts the identified Azure service code to the equivalent AWS SDK calls, and validates that the changes are incorporated into the transformed code. The feature supports conversion of Azure Functions to AWS Lambda functions, Azure Blob Storage to Amazon S3, and Azure Queue Storage to Amazon SQS, with Azure Cosmos DB to Amazon DynamoDB conversion available in preview.

AWS Transform is available in eight AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), Asia Pacific (Mumbai, Tokyo, Seoul, Sydney), Canada (Central), and Europe (Frankfurt, London).

To learn more, see Convert cloud-native code to AWS in the AWS Transform User Guide.

items.title: Amazon Braket now in scope for FedRAMP Class C
items.summary:
Amazon Braket is now in scope for FedRAMP Class C in AWS US Regions where Braket is available. The Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP) is a US government-wide program that delivers a standard approach to the security assessment, authorization, and continuous monitoring of cloud products and services.

With FedRAMP Class C authorization, government customers and the organizations that serve them can use Amazon Braket to explore quantum computing within an authorized boundary. The AWS-operated components of Braket, including the API and SDK, job orchestration and management, compilation, and result storage in Amazon S3, are within the FedRAMP-certified boundary, while quantum workloads execute on third-party Quantum Hardware Providers (QHPs) outside that boundary. All data sent to QHPs meets AWS' privacy and security requirements including removal of all personally identifiable information, data encryption in transit and at rest, and adherence to AWS' standard data retention and deletion policies.

To learn more about FedRAMP, visit AWS FedRAMP services and the FedRAMP Marketplace. To learn more about Amazon Braket, visit the Braket product page and Getting Started on Braket resources.

Regional Availability: US East (N. Virginia), US West (N. California), US West (Oregon)

items.title: Second-generation AWS Outposts racks now supported in the AWS Mexico (Central) Region
items.summary:
Second-generation AWS Outposts racks are now supported in the AWS Mexico (Central) Region. Outposts racks extend AWS infrastructure, AWS services, APIs, and tools to virtually any on-premises data center or colocation space for a truly consistent hybrid experience. 
 
Organizations of every size, from startups to enterprises to public sector agencies, can now order Outposts racks connected to this newly supported Region to optimize for latency and data residency needs. This regional expansion provides additional flexibility in the number of AWS Regions that customers’ Outposts can connect to.

To learn more about second-generation Outposts racks, read the blog post and the user guide. For the latest list of countries and territories and the AWS Regions where second-generation Outposts racks are supported, see the Outposts rack FAQs page.

items.title: AWS End User Messaging adds registration improvements for faster, higher-quality submissions
items.summary:
AWS End User Messaging now makes it easier to complete messaging registrations correctly the first time, with clearer guidance, explicit field requirements, and help avoiding the most common rejection reasons. Registrations ask for compliance evidence such as opt-in proof and sample messages, and submissions are often delayed or denied when that evidence is incomplete or a required field is missed. These improvements give you worked examples, surface exactly which fields you must provide, and walk you through the content that most often causes denials.

First, example mock-ups of a compliant opt-in and sample messages are now included for US 10DLC, US short code, US toll-free and RCS registrations, so you can see what a compliant submission looks like before you build your own. Second, the registration API response now surfaces conditional logic, so you and your AI agents no longer have to guess which fields are required based on other field values. The response tells you which fields are required for your specific registration. Third, RCS registration now includes a walkthrough for recording the compliant video that agent registrations require.

These improvements are available in all Regions where AWS End User Messaging registrations are available.

To learn more and get started, see the End User Messaging User Guide.

items.title: AWS End User Messaging now supports Brand Profiles
items.summary:
Today, AWS End User Messaging announces Brand Profiles, which let you store your brand and company information once and reuse it across your messaging registrations. To send messages on SMS, RCS, and WhatsApp, you register your brand with carriers and messaging providers, and today you fill in the same company details, address, contact information, and use case by hand on every form, for each channel and country. That repeated entry slows every new registration, and a typo or other error can get one rejected and delay when you can start sending. With Brand Profiles, you enter this information once and apply it to each new registration, so you register faster and keep your details consistent across channels and countries. You can use Brand Profiles whether you send for your own brand or manage several brands in a single AWS account.

When you start a registration with a Brand Profile, the service fills in the matching fields from the information you saved and gives you a draft to review before you submit. By default, it matches standard fields such as company name, tax ID, address, and contact details. You can also turn on smart match, which uses AI to fill in fields even when their names differ. You can build a Brand Profile from scratch or start from your existing registrations.

Brand Profiles is available in all commercial AWS Regions where AWS End User Messaging is available.

To learn more and get started, see the AWS End User Messaging User Guide.

items.title: AWS End User Messaging adds a guided wizard for RCS registration videos
items.summary:
Today, AWS End User Messaging adds a wizard that orchestrates the entire video capture for your RCS agent registration. RCS registrations in multiple countries, including the United States, require a screen recording that demonstrates your messaging experience. To record it, you have to send a specific sequence of messages to a test device, and until now you scripted those messages yourself, which easily introduced errors and made a mismatched or incomplete video one of the hardest parts of registering for RCS.

The wizard now drives each step of the capture for you, sending the right messages in the right order, so you record a compliant video the first time and get your agent approved sooner. The wizard is on all RCS registration forms that require a video submission.

To learn more and get started, see the AWS End User Messaging User Guide.

items.title: AWS End User Messaging now offers managed OTP verification end-to-end
items.summary:
Today, AWS End User Messaging announces end-to-end managed one-time passcode (OTP) verification in Notify. You get a working OTP solution in under five minutes, including AWS phone numbers and code verification, without setting up a phone number, registering with carriers, or managing how messages are delivered. Before, you generated the passcode yourself and passed it to Notify to send, and you built and maintained the logic to create, store, and expire codes. Now Notify generates the code, delivers it, and verifies the code the recipient enters, so you ship a complete verification flow and skip that work entirely. You can deliver codes over text, voice, and now WhatsApp.

You set the rules once in a notify code configuration: the code type, length, how long it stays valid, and how many attempts a recipient gets, along with your templates for each channel. From then on, one call sends a code to a recipient on the channel you choose, and another checks the code they enter.

Notify is available in all commercial AWS Regions where AWS End User Messaging is available.

To learn more and get started, see the AWS End User Messaging User Guide.

items.title: Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore expands to AWS GovCloud and 3 Regions
items.summary:
Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now available in four additional AWS Regions: US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Sydney), and AWS GovCloud (US-West). Web Search is a fully managed tool that provides AI agents with current grounding from the web, enabling more accurate and up-to-date responses for tasks such as research, summarization, and question answering.

With this expansion, customers can build agents that retrieve web information closer to their applications and end users with lower latency. Customers with government workloads can now use Web Search in the AWS GovCloud (US-West) Region to meet compliance and data residency requirements. 

To learn more about Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, see the Web Search tool documentation. To learn about pricing, visit Amazon Bedrock AgentCore pricing. For Region availability, visit Supported AWS Regions.

items.title: Amazon SageMaker Studio simplifies getting started for new AI/ML builders with new sign-in options
items.summary:
Amazon SageMaker Studio now lets new customers sign up with their Google, GitHub, or Apple credentials and land inside a fully configured Studio environment - no traditional AWS account setup and no console navigation required.

Previously, new customers who discovered a model on Hugging Face or an AWS product page had to complete a multi-step AWS account creation process, provide a credit card, navigate the AWS Console to find SageMaker AI, configure an environment, and set up IAM permissions before they could begin working. With earlier launches, we reduced environment setup to twenty seconds, pre-configured model customization permissions, and introduced deep links from Hugging Face and AWS product pages so customers could land directly inside Studio with a model pre-loaded. Now, with new sign-in options, customers complete a simplified sign-up using an existing identity, receive free credits as part of the AWS Free Tier with no credit card required in most cases, and arrive inside a ready-to-use SageMaker Studio environment where they can immediately fine-tune, evaluate, and deploy foundation models. Customers can invite team members by email, and collaborators sign in with their own email credentials to access the shared Studio environment, including shared models, notebooks, and endpoints without configuring IAM users or permissions. When a project grows beyond free credits, customers can upgrade to a paid plan and set a spend limit to stay within budget. Verified customers continue to receive default GPU access to G5, G6, G6e, and G4dn instances across endpoint deployments, training jobs, and notebooks without requesting quota increases.

This feature is available in all AWS Commercial Regions where Amazon SageMaker Studio is supported. To get started, visit any supported model on Hugging Face and select "Customize and Deploy on SageMaker AI" or "Deploy on SageMaker AI," or click Get Started from the SageMaker Studio page. To learn more, see the AWS sign-up documentation and SageMaker Studio setup guide.

items.title: Amazon EC2 T8i instances are now available in South America (São Paulo)
items.summary:
Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) T8i instances are now available in South America (São Paulo). These instances are powered by custom sixth generation Intel Xeon 6 processors, available exclusively on AWS, and built on the latest sixth generation AWS Nitro cards. T8i instances deliver up to 30% better price performance compared to previous generation T3 instances, and offer four sizes: nano, micro, small, and medium. These instances are designed for workloads requiring low to moderate CPU utilization, including data processing, login gateways, small databases, batch processing, event driven functions, CI/CD pipelines, microservices, and low traffic websites.

T8i instances deliver up to 70% higher compute performance, 1.25x higher network bandwidth, and 2.4x higher EBS bandwidth compared to T3 instances. They use the same CPU credit system as T3 with Standard and Unlimited modes, so existing T3 customers can upgrade to T8i and immediately benefit from better price performance, enabling them to lower their TCO. For customers new to AWS or migrating from on-premises, T8i instances provide one of the most cost-effective entry points to run a variety of workloads.

T8i.micro and T8i.small are available under the AWS Free Tier. T8i instances are available in US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (Oregon, N. California), Europe (Frankfurt, Ireland, London, Paris), Asia Pacific (Hyderabad, Malaysia, Mumbai, Seoul, Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo), Canada (Central) and South America (São Paulo) regions. T8i instances are available to purchase via On-Demand instances, and Spot instances with Savings Plan option coming soon. To learn more, visit the Amazon EC2 T8i instances page.

items.title: AWS Transform for migrations is now available in Asia Pacific (Singapore)
items.summary:
AWS Transform for migrations is now available in the Asia Pacific (Singapore) Region, giving customers data residency within the region and lower latency to local source infrastructure as they migrate. AWS Transform is a collaborative enterprise IT transformation service powered by agentic AI that accelerates cloud migration, application modernization, and continuous tech debt reduction.

With AWS Transform for migrations, enterprise IT teams can automate the entire migration lifecycle, from discovery and wave planning through network conversion and launching test and cutover instances, using purpose-built AI agents. The service supports infrastructure migration for workloads from virtually any source, including VMware, Hyper-V, KVM, bare metal, and hybrid environments, unifying teams, tools, and workflows in a single collaborative workbench.

To get started, see the AWS Transform documentation or visit the AWS Transform product page.

items.title: Amazon DynamoDB Streams now supports timestamp-based stream processing
items.summary:
Amazon DynamoDB Streams now supports timestamp-based stream processing, enabling you to begin reading stream records from a specific point in time. Previously, you could only start from the oldest retained record (up to 24 hours old) or from new records written after you start consuming the stream. Now, you can supply a timestamp and begin processing at the first record written at or after that time using the AT_TIMESTAMP shard iterator type.

Timestamp-based stream processing can be used with the Amazon Kinesis Client Library (KCL) through the DynamoDB Streams Kinesis adapter. It helps you avoid reprocessing entire retained streams or missing records when resuming stream consumption, supporting common use cases such as recovery after an interruption, data replay for debugging and auditing by reading from a specific point in the past, skipping a backlog by resuming from a recent timestamp near the latest records, and synchronizing after a restore by beginning at the export timestamp following a point-in-time recovery (PITR) export.

Timestamp-based stream processing is available in all commercial AWS Regions, the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, and the China Regions. There is no additional charge for this feature beyond standard GetRecords API request charges. To get started, see Amazon DynamoDB Streams timestamp documentation in the DynamoDB developer guide.

items.title: AWS がネットワークスキャンのガイドラインを導入
items.summary: AWS は、お客様のワークロードを対象としたネットワークスキャンのガイドラインを導入します。ネットワークスキャンは正当なセキュリティ目的にも、脅威アクターによる偵察にも使われ、両者を見分けるのは困難です。本記事では、セキュリティデータに利害を持つさまざまな関係者を整理します。そのうえで、ガイドラインに準拠したスキャナーが従うべき 4 つの原則 (観察のみ、識別可能、協調的、機密保持) と、準拠によって得られるメリットを紹介します。

items.title: AWS におけるサイバーレジリエンスと事業継続のためのプロアクティブな戦略
items.summary: ランサムウェアなどのサイバーセキュリティインシデントや自然災害に備え、公共部門の組織が AWS でワークロードを復旧できるよう準備するためのプロアクティブな戦略を紹介します。NIST CSF 2.0 や AWS Well-Architected フレームワークを踏まえ、マルチアカウント戦略と、Infrastructure as Code (IaC) によるインフラストラクチャ構築の自動化を解説します。さらに、AZ ID やマルチリージョンを活用した復旧用アカウントの準備、AWS Backup によるバックアップ、復旧用アカウントでの自動テストについても説明します。

items.title: AWS Security Incident Response: インシデント対応ライフサイクルを加速するためのお客様の取り組み
items.summary: AWS Security Incident Response がインシデント対応ライフサイクルのあらゆる段階をどのように加速するのかを、ランサムウェアの可能性がある不審なアクティビティへの対応シナリオを通じて紹介します。Amazon GuardDuty や AWS Security Hub と統合した自動トリアージ、AWS Systems Manager による自動封じ込め、AWS Security Incident Response Engineering (SIRE) チームへのエスカレーション、インシデントケース ID を使ったタグ付けなど、検出から解決までの流れを解説します。あわせて、アラート疲れを軽減し、対応時間を短縮する方法も説明します。

items.title: AWS Security Incident Response によるセキュリティ運用の最適化
items.summary: この記事では、AWS Security Incident Response を有効にして概念実証 (POC) を実施し、セキュリティ運用を迅速に強化する方法を説明します。まず、Amazon GuardDuty の検出結果と、AWS Security Hub でサードパーティ製ツールから取り込む一部の検出結果を自動でトリアージする仕組みを紹介します。次に、成功基準の設定、委任管理者やエスカレーションなどの構成の定義、デプロイの準備、コンソールでの有効化手順を順に解説します。さらに、初日からリアクティブ機能を活用し、疑わしいアクティビティがある場合は AWS がサポートするケースを作成して、AWS の専門家の支援を受けながら価値を最大化する方法も紹介します。

items.title: Kiro はどのように自らを修正し、その修正の正しさをどう担保しているか
items.summary: Kiro のファイル読み取りツールと検索ツールの説明に、ハーネスの動作について事実と異なる主張をする一文がありました。この一文は数百のセッションで 61,742 回モデルに届いていました。何の役にも立っておらず、誰かがチケットを起票することもまずなかったでしょう。こうした問題は見つけるのが難しく、修正の良し悪しを判断するのも同じくらい難しいものです。たとえば私たちは、より多くのタスクに合格し、使用トークンも少ない修正をあやうくリリースするところでした。結果をホストごとに分けてみると、改善のほぼすべてが、エージェントがいつもはまり込むループからたまたま抜け出した 1 回の実行によるものだとわかったのです。そのホストを除くと、その修正は遅く、コストが高く、精度も下がっていました。自分の修正を自分で採点するループなら、これをリリースしていたでしょう。

items.title: Kiro IDE と CLI にメモリ機能が登場
items.summary: 本日、Kiro IDE と CLI にメモリ機能を導入します。Kiro は、あなたが好む作業の進め方、リポジトリ固有のコマンドや規約、受けた訂正、デバッグで得た知見、すでに除外したアプローチを覚えておけるようになります。それらが再び関係する場面になると、Kiro はあなたのコンテキストを引き継ぎます。コンテキストを説明し直したり同じ訂正を繰り返したりする時間が減り、Kiro は言われなくてもあなたの好みに沿って動けるようになり、使い込むほど役に立つ存在になります。

items.title: AWS DevOps Agent で調査コストを事前に制御する
items.summary: AWS DevOps Agent のような自律型 AI エージェントは、調査中に呼び出す API、回数、対象スコープを動的に判断します。そのため、調査能力だけでなく、実行前にコストを把握して制御する仕組みも重要です。Investigation Cost Guardrail スキルを利用すると、最初の課金対象クエリを実行する前に見積もりを確認し、続行するかどうかを判断できます。本記事では、このオープンソーススキルが AWS サービスやサードパーティーツールの操作を分類し、リージョンごとのライブ料金とデータ転送コストを取得する仕組みを解説します。また、Proceed（続行）、Warn（警告）、Halt（停止）の判定ゲートを、3 つの具体的な調査シナリオとともに紹介します。

items.title: Amazon Bedrock と LiteLLM による OpenAI ChatGPT Codex の予算・レート制限管理
items.summary: OpenAI ChatGPT Codex のモデル推論を Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) 上の LiteLLM ゲートウェイ経由で Amazon Bedrock にルーティングし、生成 AI コーディングエージェントをエンタープライズ向けに一元管理する方法を紹介します。AWS Fargate へのデプロイ手順、スコープ付きキーによる予算とレート制限の適用、Responses API の互換性検証を解説します。AWS IAM Identity Center による直接アクセスや Portkey を使用する代替アクセス経路も取り上げます。

items.title: スピードと安全性の両立: AI コーディングエージェントのためのコントロールフレームワーク
items.summary: Kiro などの AI コーディングエージェントは開発を加速させる一方で、プロンプトインジェクションや過度に緩い設定、サプライチェーンリスク、スコープクリープなどのリスクをもたらします。本記事では、IDE でエージェントの出力を方向付ける作成時のコントロールと、パイプラインで検証するビルド時のコントロールの 2 つの柱からなるアプリケーションセキュリティのフレームワークを紹介します。決定論的な緩和策、非決定論的な緩和策、人間によるレビューの組み合わせ方に加えて、Kiro、AWS CodeBuild、AWS CodePipeline を使用した実装例も解説します。

items.title: Amazon Linux で npm と pip のパッケージ更新を安全にする方法
items.summary: npm や PyPI のパッケージは、公開直後の数時間に最もサプライチェーンのリスクが高くなります。この記事では、Amazon Linux 2023 で npm の min-release-age と pip の uploaded-prior-to を使用して 1 日の依存関係のクールダウンを設定し、予期しないパッケージのインストールを防ぐ方法を紹介します。また、npm audit と pip-audit で特定したパッケージに限ってクールダウンをオーバーライドし、セキュリティ修正を適用する方法も説明します。
